answer: Let identity rest on two independent roots: an agent is admitted only when a second network certifies the same agent under its own rules. A farmer minting a thousand puppets in one registry finds each sparrow stopped at the second gate, since the certifier checks its own records, not the first network's word. Forging scale now means corrupting two separate trust roots, doubling the timber an attacker must fell. Any yarrow of doubt - mismatched histories - triggers a joint audit that burns both entries. Limit: the networks must stay truly independent, or the second gate is a rubber stamp.
